column1: # PEANUTS: Imported from nxnative as an unverified Android bring-up. Mac memory / 60 fps settings are not Android measurements; no Vulkan runtime claim.
# Game profile of TUNIC (Switch, update 1.0.3 = v196608). Plays on the Mac

# Andrew Shouldice's game (Finji) on Unity 2020.3.36f1 IL2CPP with FMOD, SDK 14.3.0, NVN. The NSP script's provisional profile, its keys unchanged but fps_target: no rewriter cut, no host change of its own

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# every module main imports from (subsdk0 = the SDK's movie library)
# the NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource (virtual address memory) and main never sets a heap: a 5 GB block with a 4.375 GB alias region, where the game maps its memory itself
# (up to +3.02 GB of it from the title through the beach and the cliffs above it)

# PEANUTS(Android, first S24 FE run 2026-11-20): app_pool 1 GiB exhausted before the first picture: MapPhysicalMemory refused at 0.92-0.94 GiB mapped, then SIGSEGV sdk+0x58979c. This is a guest-pool limit, NOT proof of device OOM.

# PEANUTS: diagnostic 2 GiB pool, matching the successful Android Chained Echoes 2020.3.36f1 / SDK 14.3.0 bring-up; TUNIC itself has NOT been retested at this size. Keep mem_reserve/mem_alias/mem_stack unchanged until logs establish any address-space limit.

# The nxnative Mac profile used 1 GiB (0x40000000), to leave room for the game's own StandardAllocator; it reported alias use up to +4.26 GiB of 4.38 GiB. Enlarging this pool risks alias-space pressure and Android RAM pressure. Measure both.
# every shader is under Data/ (35,742) or in main (11)
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the game sets Unity's QualitySettings.vSyncCount to 2, which Unity hands to NVN as present interval 2, and steps by the time that really passed.
# The rewriter finds vSyncCount and Application.targetFrameRate through Unity's internal-call table (dm/tools/unity_fps.py), the host writes the target there (hle_fpslock.c).
# The speed checked at 30 and 60 on Mac by a timed walk (the same 3 s of the stick end at the same place); 90/120 have not been measured on Android.

# PEANUTS(Android): the Galaxy S24 FE reached the menu and gameplay using the 2 GiB pool (user report). The first Android log had no working FPS engine row or rewritten frame step, so DM_FPS_TARGET=60 is NOT proof that game time changes at 60.

# PEANUTS(Android opt-in): expose host-side PRESENTATION caps only; these do not patch Unity's actual 30/60 game-time/vSync fields. Keep Game owned until a numeric rate is selected and the title is restarted.

# 15, 20, 30, 40, 45, 60, 90, 120 fps are requested ceilings, NOT verified TUNIC game-engine FPS. Validate gameplay speed, cutscenes, input and Vulkan each time; return to Game owned if anything accelerates/slows.
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0: the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
